findings.finding: Memory for verbal information is improved when a relevant visual is presented alongside it.
findings.quote: memory for some verbal information is enhanced if a relevant visual is also presented

findings.finding: Visual information can be enhanced when paired with relevant verbal information.
findings.quote: visual information can often be enhanced when paired with relevant verbal information

findings.finding: Spoken words and sentences lead to improved memory when they are paired with a real or imagined image.
findings.quote: participants had improved memory for spoken words and sentences when paired with an image, imagined or real

principle: Information is processed and remembered better when it uses both verbal and visual channels, combining words and images.
for_the_teacher: Pair spoken instructions and step names with visual demonstrations or mental images.
when_it_does_not_apply: Dual coding theory does not take into account the possibility of cognition being mediated by something other than words and images, and is only valid for tests on which people are asked to focus on identifying how concepts are related.
